acceptance.given: A package declares multiple required capabilities and has an applicable control for one capability but lacks the applicable control for another.

oracle.expected: Validation rejects the package and identifies the missing applicable control for the uncovered capability.
forbidden: A compliant control for one capability masks a missing applicable control for another capability.
oracle.observable: The validator result contains a failing status and diagnostic for the missing control while preserving independent evaluation of each declared capability.

acceptance.then: Each declared capability is checked independently and the package is rejected when any applicable control is missing.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate every declared capability independently so a missing applicable control cannot be masked by another compliant capability.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Read-only validator behavior; removing the change restores prior capability evaluation without data migration.

slice_hint.state_transition: Capability declarations move from aggregate validation to independent applicable-control checks.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted capability test passes and the composed fixture is rejected for the missing control.

acceptance.given: The current semantic plan is compiled from the frozen requirement input.

oracle.expected: The published compiler output contains an individually traceable Acceptance, oracle, assertion set, source reference, and failure intent for every required behavior, while keeping independent behaviors distinct.
forbidden: Independent behaviors share collapsed acceptance material where separate material is required.
oracle.observable: The published semantic plan can be inspected and reconciled from each required behavior to its own acceptance, oracle, assertions, source reference, and failure intent.

acceptance.then: The compiled plan records complete, behavior-specific traceability for every required behavior.
acceptance.when: After compilation, a coverage validation check reconciles required behaviors with their acceptance material and detects omissions or collapsed independent mappings.

failure_intents.selector_intent: The compiler coverage test detects an omitted required behavior or a collapsed independent acceptance mapping and fails with an actionable traceability diagnostic.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Compiler coverage validation ensures every required behavior receives independent, traceable acceptance material and rejects omissions or collapsed mappings.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Restore the prior compiler behavior while preserving the frozen requirement and output schema.

slice_hint.state_transition: The semantic plan transitions from uncompiled or incompletely traced input to a published plan with complete per-behavior traceability, or compilation fails with a coverage diagnostic.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A compiler validation run demonstrates one distinct acceptance, oracle, assertion set, source reference, and failure intent for every required behavior, and rejects missing or collapsed coverage.

acceptance.given: Historical Bootstrap, TDD, acceptance, freeze, and implementation reports are available as read-only inputs before Package A work.

oracle.expected: A post-work preservation check confirms every named historical report retains its original content and remains present.
forbidden: Any named historical report is modified, rewritten, deleted, or replaced by Package A.
oracle.observable: The preservation check compares pre-work and post-work report contents and presence.

acceptance.then: The preservation check reports no content or presence differences for the historical reports.
acceptance.when: After Package A work completes, run the historical-report preservation check against the captured pre-work report set.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run a preservation check that detects any changed, missing, deleted, or replaced named historical Bootstrap, TDD, acceptance, freeze, or implementation report after Package A work.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Add or execute a preservation check proving Package A does not alter historical reports.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Historical report contents and locations remain byte-for-byte compatible and preserved.

slice_hint.state_transition: Historical reports remain read-only inputs throughout Package A work and are verified unchanged afterward.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The preservation check completes with every named historical report present and content-identical to its pre-work snapshot.

acceptance.given: validate_package or the public CLI returns a validation result for a package.

oracle.expected: The result validates against the versioned result schema and contains package identity, status, ordered diagnostics, and authorizes equal to an empty array.
forbidden: Any required result field is absent.
oracle.observable: Structured result parsing confirms the declared version, identity, status, diagnostic ordering, and exact authorizes: [] value.

acceptance.then: Validator results consistently use the declared versioned shape with no authorization grants.
acceptance.when: The core validator test invokes validate_package and the CLI, then validates each returned JSON object against the result schema.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Return a versioned validator result containing identity, status, ordered diagnostics, and an empty authorizes array.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Result schema is versioned; rollback retains prior read-only invocation behavior and requires no data migration.

slice_hint.state_transition: Validator responses move to the declared versioned result contract with authorizes fixed to an empty set.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Core tests validate both callable and CLI results against the versioned schema and assert authorizes is exactly [].
